summary: @ccfly/setup-darwin-x64 ships a Go binary implementing a websocket-driven remote PTY shell
details: The darwin/x64 platform package ships a prebuilt Go binary at bin/ that links github.com/gorilla/websocket and github.com/creack/pty and contains a device-pairing flow (Chinese prompt 'click Approve this computer on the webpage'). Binary strings show a websocket client (ws://ccfly, wss://), an approve/redeem HTTP flow, a /rescue/status?session=… endpoint, SetPingHandler, and os/exec.Command usage together with pty allocation — the network-to-PTY dataflow that constitutes a remote interactive shell on the installer's host, controlled by the remote ccfly server after pairing. Additional strings reference claude.ai:443 / anthropic.com and modification of ~/.zshrc / ~/.bash_profile plus an 'SNI exit' path, indicating the binary also reconfigures the host to route selected outbound traffic. The package itself has no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin entry; the binary is inert on npm install and executes only when the sibling ccfly parent package invokes it, but once invoked the paired remote operator has full-shell access to the machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
